mainTopic: The end of the story of רמי בר תמרי in רב חסדא's town, and אביי's question about whether cooked liver (כבדא) makes other meat forbidden.
overview: This amud finishes the story of רמי בר תמרי in the town of רב חסדא. First he explains why he wore a garment without ציצית: a borrowed טלית is exempt for thirty days. Then a man who did not honor his parents is brought in to be flogged. רמי בר תמרי stops it with a ברייתא: a positive מצוה whose reward is written next to it in the Torah is not enforced by an earthly court. רב חסדא praises his sharpness. The גמרא then turns to liver. אביי asks רב ספרא to find out how the sages of ארץ ישראל treat it, and רב זריקא reports that he cooked liver for רבי אמי, who ate it. אביי says this misses his point: he wants to know whether liver makes other meat in the pot forbidden. רב ספרא challenges him from a משנה that seems to answer this, and אביי begins to reply that the משנה may be about forbidden liver. His answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A borrowed garment is exempt from ציצית for thirty days
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר תמרי explains why he wore a garment without ציצית: a borrowed טלית is exempt for the first thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: A borrowed robe, for all of the first thirty days, is exempt from ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר תמרי is answering רב חסדא's question about why he was wearing a four-cornered garment without ציצית. His answer: the garment was borrowed, and a borrowed טלית is exempt for thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garment does not belong to him, so for a limited time the obligation of ציצית does not apply. The exemption has a time limit of thirty days. So this is not a general rule that borrowed garments never need ציצית; it is a temporary exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: The fringes the Torah requires on a four-cornered garment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a borrowed garment is never obligated. The exemption only lasts thirty days.

phrases.english: A borrowed robe,
for all of the first thirty days,
is exempt from ציצית.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַלִּית שְׁאוּלָה כׇּל שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם פְּטוּרָה מִן הַצִּיצִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's question from before this section about the garment without ציצית.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The garment was borrowed, and a borrowed טלית is exempt from ציצית for thirty days.

steps.title: A man who did not honor his parents is brought for punishment
steps.stepSummary: While they were talking, a man who did not honor his father and mother was brought in and tied up to be flogged.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, they brought in a certain man who did not honor his father and his mother, and they tied him up.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to a new scene. A man who did not honor his parents is brought to רב חסדא's court and tied up for flogging. This sets up רמי בר תמרי's next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is argued yet; this only describes the scene. The court is about to punish a man for failing to keep the מצוה of honoring parents. The next step will challenge whether the court may do this at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Meanwhile, in the middle of this
They tied him up (to be flogged)

phrases.english: Meanwhile,
they brought in a certain man
who would not honor his father and his mother,
and they tied him up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same story with a new incident in רב חסדא's court.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who did not honor his parents was tied up to be flogged.

steps.title: A court does not enforce a מצוה whose reward is written next to it
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר תמרי tells them to release the man. He quotes a ברייתא: a positive מצוה whose reward is written alongside it is not enforced by an earthly court.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Leave him alone. For it is taught in a ברייתא: any positive מצוה whose reward is stated next to it, the court below is not commanded to enforce it.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר תמרי stops the flogging. He brings a ברייתא to prove that the court has no right to punish someone for not honoring his parents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Honoring parents is a מצות עשה, and the Torah writes its reward right next to it (long life). The ברייתא says that when the Torah states the reward next to a positive מצוה, the earthly court is not told to enforce it. So the punishment is left to Heaven, and this man should not be flogged.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave him alone, let him go
A positive commandment (something you must actively do)
Its reward is written right next to it in the Torah
The earthly court (as opposed to the Heavenly court)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known rule about the limits of a court's power to enforce certain positive מצוות, and כיבוד אב ואם is the classic example.

phrases.english: He said to them: Leave him alone,
phrases.notes: The speaker is רמי בר תמרי.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a ברייתא:
any positive מצוה
whose reward is stated alongside it –
phrases.notes: For honoring parents, the reward is long life, written right after it in דברים 5:16.

phrases.english: the court below is not
commanded to enforce it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the court's action in step 2 with a proof from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the man who did not honor his parents should not be flogged by the court.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a positive מצוה whose reward is stated alongside it is not enforced by the earthly court.

steps.title: רב חסדא praises רמי בר תמרי's sharpness
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells רמי בר תמרי that he is very sharp. רמי בר תמרי answers that in רב יהודה's place he could show his sharpness even more.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: I see that you are very sharp. He answered him: If you were in the place of רב יהודה, I would show you my sharpness.
steps.whatsHappening: The story closes. רב חסדא admits that רמי בר תמרי has answered well, and רמי בר תמרי replies that he could show even more sharpness in רב יהודה's place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By praising him, רב חסדא accepts all of רמי בר תמרי's answers, including the last one about the man. רמי בר תמרי's reply suggests he could show his abilities better in רב יהודה's town than here.

keyTerms.meaning: In his place, in his town

steps.whatToRemember: רמי בר תמרי defended every one of his unusual actions with a source. רב חסדא ended up praising his sharpness.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב חסדא is speaking to רמי בר תמרי.

phrases.english: I see that you are very sharp.
He said to him:
If you were in the place of רב יהודה,
I would show you my sharpness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ חֲזֵינָא לָךְ דְּחָרִיפַתְּ טוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story after רמי בר תמרי's successful defense in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב חסדא accepts רמי בר תמרי's answers and recognizes how sharp he is.

steps.title: אביי asks how the sages of ארץ ישראל treat liver
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב ספרא to find out, when he goes up to ארץ ישראל, how the sages there treat liver.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב ספרא: When you go up there, ask them: Liver, how do you treat it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about local practices. אביי sends a question with רב ספרא to the sages of ארץ ישראל about liver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liver is a special case because it is full of blood. אביי wants to know how the sages in ארץ ישראל handle it in practice. This step sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: You go up there (to ארץ ישראל)
What do you do with it, how do you treat it

phrases.english: אביי said to רב ספרא:
When you go up there,
ask them:
Liver, how do you treat it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב סָפְרָא: כִּי סָלְקַתְּ לְהָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still about how practices differ from place to place.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the sages of ארץ ישראל treat liver.

steps.title: רב זריקא cooked liver for רבי אמי and he ate it
steps.stepSummary: When רב ספרא went up, he found רב זריקא. רב זריקא told him that he cooked liver for רבי אמי, and רבי אמי ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he went up, he found רב זריקא. He said to him: I cooked liver for רבי אמי, and he ate it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא brings אביי's question to ארץ ישראל. רב זריקא answers with a real-life example: he cooked liver for רבי אמי, and רבי אמי ate it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of stating a rule, רב זריקא answers with something that actually happened. A great sage like רבי אמי ate liver that was cooked, so cooking liver was accepted in practice there.

phrases.english: When he went up,
phrases.notes: רב ספרא went up to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: he found רב זריקא.
He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב זריקא is answering אביי's question.

phrases.english: I cooked liver for רבי אמי,
and he ate it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Liver may be cooked and eaten: רב זריקא cooked it for רבי אמי, who ate it.

steps.title: אביי explains that the report does not answer his real question
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the case of רבי אמי eating liver cooked alone does not help. He never asked whether liver forbids itself. He asked whether it forbids other meat cooked with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב ספרא came back to אביי, אביי said to him: I never asked whether liver makes itself forbidden. My question is whether it makes another piece of meat forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא returns with the story about רבי אמי, and אביי pushes it aside. That story answers a question he never asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי ate liver that was cooked by itself. That only shows the liver does not soak back up its own blood. אביי wants to know something else: does the blood that comes out of the liver soak into other meat in the same pot and make it forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: Its fellow, meaning another piece of meat cooked together with it
I have a question about it, I am unsure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two questions. 'Forbids itself' means the liver becomes forbidden. 'Forbids its fellow' means other food in the pot becomes forbidden. אביי only asked about the second.

phrases.english: When he came to him,
phrases.notes: רב ספרא came back from ארץ ישראל to אביי with the report.

phrases.english: he said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לְמֵיסַר נַפְשַׁהּ – לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי,
phrases.english: Whether it makes itself forbidden, I am not asking about that.
What I am asking about is whether it makes another piece forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵיסַר נַפְשַׁהּ לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in Step 6 as off-target and sharpens the question from Step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The story about רבי אמי does not apply to אביי's question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story only shows that liver does not forbid itself. It says nothing about other meat in the pot.

steps.title: רב ספרא challenges: the same משנה answers both questions
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא asks: you are sure liver does not forbid itself because of a משנה. But that same משנה also says liver forbids other food. So why are you asking?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are you sure that liver does not forbid itself? Because we learned that it is not made forbidden. Then do not ask about it forbidding other food either! We learned: liver forbids other food but is not forbidden itself, because it gives out blood and does not take it in.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא challenges אביי. The source that settles one half of the question seems to settle the other half too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's certainty about 'itself' must come from the משנה that says liver 'is not made forbidden.' But that משנה says in the same breath that liver 'makes others forbidden.' So אביי's question seems to be answered by the very source he relies on.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? A challenge asking why two cases are treated differently

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea in this משנה, that liver gives out blood but does not take it in, explains how liver is treated when it is cooked with other food.

phrases.english: What is different about it making itself forbidden
that you have no question about it?
Because we learned: it is not made forbidden.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in תרומות 10:11, quoted in full below.

phrases.aramaic: לְמֵיסַר חֲבִירְתַּהּ נָמֵי לָא תִּבְּעֵי לָךְ!
phrases.english: Then about it making another piece forbidden, you should have no question either!
For we learned: Liver makes other food forbidden but is not made forbidden,
because it gives out and does not take in.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא לְמֵיסַר נַפְשַׁהּ דְּלָא מִיבַּעְיָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's claim in Step 7 that the 'other meat' question is still open.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that whether liver forbids other meat is still an open question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same משנה that shows liver is not forbidden itself also says plainly that it forbids other food. So the question is already answered.

steps.title: אביי answers: the משנה may be about forbidden liver
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins his answer. The משנה may only be talking about liver that was forbidden to begin with, so it does not answer his question about kosher liver.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Perhaps there, the משנה is talking about forbidden liver.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts to defend his question. He limits the משנה to a narrower case. The answer continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the liver itself is forbidden, for example from a non-kosher animal, then it is obvious that it can make other food forbidden. That would not tell us what kosher liver does to other meat, so אביי's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden liver, liver that was forbidden from the start

phrases.english: He said to him: Perhaps there
it is about forbidden liver,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 8 by limiting the משנה to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the משנה is about a narrower situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's rule that liver forbids other food applies to all liver, including kosher liver.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה may only be about forbidden liver, so the question about kosher liver stays open (the answer continues in the next part).
